note: Extra US tariff on China-made laptops from week 0 of the fiscal year (scenario; 20% was paid Mar-Nov 2025)
Negotiated share of the tariff that goes into the channel price. Pass-through is negotiated (Q35); 2025 outcomes ran from 67-90% (Asus, Mar 2025) to 100% (Acer, Feb 2025), so 85%

Chance that the negotiation ends with the company absorbing the tariff itself (no price rise); possible but unlikely (Q35). The cutover is chosen before the outcome, so costs are expected over the two cases
Weeks from the tariff to the new channel price; the brand absorbs the tariff until then (10% tariff on 4 Feb 2025, Acer price rise reported 18 Feb)
Share of a US tariff absorbed by foreign exporters through lower prices; the importer pays the rest (Kiel Institute: about 4%)
Weeks for the new site to cover the region's volume after cutover, linear; China builds the rest and pays the tariff (Module 3, strong GSM 8-16)

Fiscal-year shipment target (sell-in units) as a share of the pre-tariff plan. The BU must ship 100% of the target and usually beats it, so the plan sits above it: about 3% (size Q33). The annual target is not lowered unless it truly cannot be reached (Q32)
The first-half shortfall is re-phased into Q3 and Q4 (Q1 and Q2 targets lowered, Q3 or Q4 raised): the catch-up runs from this week (start of Q3) to year end

Largest channel price discount (price points) in the catch-up weeks. Planners do not know it: sales planning asks sales, and sales negotiate the points with the channel case by case (Q33); beyond it the target is lowered
Share of the catch-up price points the BU has to fund (the points may need to come from the BU), so the BU weighs it against its MWD
Share of the price points that reaches the shelf price and moves units (the channel may keep part); the BU pays the full points
1 = the company also holds the fiscal-year target (the fiscal year concerns all of the company), so it only picks among options that reach it; 0 = pure cost

Share of the claimed MWD that migrates before the year-end reconciliation (netted into other regions' builds of the same model, other models, the new site), down to the physical MWD of Module 2. Transfers move one region while the same models keep being built for other regions (Q34): only region-specific parts stay (keyboards, cords, packaging: 8% of the cancelled BOM here), so 85-95%; if a whole model or platform moved, only industry-standard parts would migrate: 45-70% by value (CPU + DRAM + SSD = 45% of a mainstream notebook BOM in 1Q25, 68% in 3Q26, TrendForce)
What one dollar of MWD that stays costs the BU after resale: brokers pay 5-15% of cost for excess components (Circuits Assembly 2025; liquidation about 12 cents on the dollar, Inbound Logistics)
New-site conversion cost uplift, midpoint of 5-10% (R20)
Parts expediting per unit while the +4 week lead time is not yet covered, strong GSM (Module 3)
